en: The hottest part of the day is usually around 3 PM, not noon, because Earth's surface needs hours to absorb and re-radiate the sun's heat.
Lightning can strike the same place many times; tall structures like the Empire State Building get hit by lightning about 25 times every year.
Volcanic soil, like that found near Taal Volcano in Batangas, is extremely fertile because it contains mineral-rich ash from past eruptions.
Talc is the softest mineral on the Mohs hardness scale and can be easily scratched by a fingernail, proving not all minerals are hard.
The water you drink today is the same water that has been recycled through Earth's water cycle for billions of years, not newly created water.
The Sun is not on fire; it produces energy through nuclear fusion, a process that combines hydrogen atoms into helium in its extremely hot core.
A star's color reveals its surface temperature; blue stars like Rigel are much hotter than red stars like Betelgeuse.
The Moon does not produce its own light; the bright glow we see at night is sunlight reflecting off the Moon's rocky surface.
Earthquakes begin at a deep underground point called the focus, which can be hundreds of kilometers below the epicenter on Earth's surface.
Typhoons form and gain strength only over warm ocean water, which is why they weaken quickly after making landfall on Philippine islands.
Rocks constantly change through the rock cycle; for example, limestone transforms into marble when subjected to extreme heat and pressure deep underground.
Earth's seasons are caused by its 23.5-degree axial tilt, not by distance from the Sun; Earth is actually closest to the Sun during January.
